ectogenesis.label: Species and observed developmental interval
ectogenesis.prompt: Record the actual entry stage, exit stage, support duration and development that occurred in a uterus. Do not convert animal gestational fractions into human ages.

ectogenesis.label: Continuity between developmental stages
ectogenesis.prompt: Identify evidence for each interface. Separate publications cannot be concatenated into a continuous IVF-to-birth demonstration.

ectogenesis.label: Exchange and placental functions
ectogenesis.prompt: Separate measured gas/nutrient/waste exchange from synthetic transport and from endocrine or immune functions.

ectogenesis.label: Growth and organ development
ectogenesis.prompt: Retain growth, morphology and organ function alongside appropriate in-utero or other comparators.

ectogenesis.label: Adverse developmental and device outcomes
ectogenesis.prompt: Record adverse findings and missing outcomes, including growth restriction, infection and blood-interface complications when assessed.

ectogenesis.label: Transition and post-support follow-up
ectogenesis.prompt: Record the exit transition, survival and duration of measured follow-up; surrogate markers do not establish lifelong outcomes.

ectogenesis.label: Applicability across models
ectogenesis.prompt: Keep species, developmental stage, specimen counts, comparator and parameter provenance visible.

ectogenesis.label: Engineering reliability and observability
ectogenesis.prompt: Label simulated power and sensor faults and all artificial thresholds; software fixture metrics are not a device safety rating.

ectogenesis.label: Complete gestation and proposed benefits
ectogenesis.prompt: Assess IVF-to-birth continuity, surrogacy replacement and congenital-anomaly reduction as separate claims requiring direct comparative evidence.

reprogramming.label: Variant and affected cell population
reprogramming.prompt: Record exact variant, allele state, assay and cell type.

reprogramming.label: Causal link to dysfunction
reprogramming.prompt: Separate association from a perturbation that changes a relevant phenotype.

reprogramming.label: Clone competition
reprogramming.prompt: Track edited and unedited clone growth, persistence and selection.

reprogramming.label: Target cell coverage
reprogramming.prompt: Record fraction reached and fraction corrected, with denominators.

reprogramming.label: Editing outcomes and genome integrity
reprogramming.prompt: Include intended edits, bystanders, off-targets and structural outcomes.

reprogramming.label: Tissue-level function
reprogramming.prompt: Prefer a functional endpoint over a molecular marker alone.

reprogramming.label: Durability
reprogramming.prompt: Record follow-up interval and whether the effect persists.

reprogramming.label: Tumor and surveillance outcomes
reprogramming.prompt: Track clonal selection, malignancy signals and impaired repair.

tissues.label: Cell identity and maturation
tissues.prompt: Record cell composition, maturation and construct architecture.

tissues.label: Perfusion and vascularization
tissues.prompt: Separate vessel patency from oxygen delivery and tissue function.

tissues.label: Host integration
tissues.prompt: Record anatomical integration, innervation and interface healing.

tissues.label: Tissue-specific function
tissues.prompt: Name the primary organ or tissue function and measurement method.

tissues.label: Donor-site cost
tissues.prompt: Record donor area, morbidity and coverage gained per donor area.

tissues.label: Adverse healing and immune response
tissues.prompt: Track rejection, thrombosis, infection, scarring and delayed closure.

tissues.label: Durability
tissues.prompt: Record duration of function and graft loss or revision.

tissues.label: Comparator and controls
tissues.prompt: Retain native-tissue, sham, standard-care or active comparators.

nanomedicine.label: Organ accumulation
nanomedicine.prompt: Record carrier and cargo separately, with dose-normalized denominators.

nanomedicine.label: Intended-cell uptake
nanomedicine.prompt: Distinguish target cell uptake from whole-organ signal.

nanomedicine.label: Intracellular cargo activity
nanomedicine.prompt: Measure editing, expression, knockdown or other direct target engagement.

nanomedicine.label: Target-cell coverage
nanomedicine.prompt: Report the fraction of intended cells with verified cargo action.

nanomedicine.label: Off-target tissue exposure
nanomedicine.prompt: Record non-target cell exposure and associated activity.

nanomedicine.label: Functional benefit
nanomedicine.prompt: Link cargo activity to a prespecified tissue function.

nanomedicine.label: Durability
nanomedicine.prompt: Separate carrier persistence from persistent biological action.

nanomedicine.label: Toxicity and tolerability
nanomedicine.prompt: Track immune effects, organ injury and adverse events by timepoint.

dental.label: Component identity and architecture
dental.prompt: Separate enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, ligament, bone and gingiva; state the measured component.

dental.label: Periodontal attachment
dental.prompt: Distinguish clinical attachment gain, bone fill and histological oriented cementum–ligament–bone attachment.

dental.label: Gingival barrier and root coverage
dental.prompt: Record root coverage, tissue phenotype, seal/barrier measurements and recurrent inflammation separately.

dental.label: Loading, occlusion and sensation
dental.prompt: Declare the mechanical or sensory assay; mineralization alone is not mastication.

dental.label: Pulp, vascular and neural integration
dental.prompt: Record living pulp, vascular supply and innervation without inferring these from a mineral image.

dental.label: Adverse healing and ectopic outcomes
dental.prompt: Retain ankylosis, root resorption, abnormal tooth number/shape, ectopic mineralization and immune findings.

dental.label: Durability
dental.prompt: Record follow-up and performance under repeated loading.

dental.label: Comparator and independent unit
dental.prompt: Distinguish patients, teeth, sites, animals and cultures; identify primary versus post hoc outcomes.

organoids.label: Cell identity and maturation
organoids.prompt: Declare the cell composition and maturation assay.

organoids.label: Transport measurements
organoids.prompt: Separate measured local oxygen from gas settings and illustrative model parameters.

organoids.label: Tissue-specific function
organoids.prompt: Use a declared function beyond markers or morphology.

organoids.label: Genome integrity and clone behavior
organoids.prompt: Separate intended genetic correction, unwanted products and clonal selection.

organoids.label: Host integration
organoids.prompt: Track perfusion, innervation and anatomical interface where relevant.

organoids.label: Persistence and adverse outcomes
organoids.prompt: Record duration, attrition and adverse findings.

organoids.label: Source, comparator and independent unit

ectogenesis.title: Complete ectogenesis capability map
ectogenesis.target: A continuous IVF-to-birth pathway outside a uterus
ectogenesis.species: Theoretical human-system ambition; animal and in-vitro source evidence remain separate
ectogenesis.hypothesis: A stage-resolved evidence map can identify the unresolved interfaces and developmental functions required to assess complete ectogenesis.
ectogenesis.endpoint: Observed developmental intervals, interface continuity, source-supported functions and explicit evidence gaps.
ectogenesis.falsifier: An apparent complete pathway depends on joining incompatible isolated systems, or assumes physiological support establishes normal development.
ectogenesis.structure_notes: The reviewed sources do not establish a continuous human IVF-to-birth system. Eliminating surrogacy and reducing birth defects remain proposed benefits. The sibling artificial-womb-models repo supplies an evidence ledger and dimensionless engineering fixtures.

evidence.value: No continuous human IVF-to-birth demonstration in the reviewed ledger
evidence.notes: FDA's 2023 discussion concerns partial support of extremely premature infants; it is not a complete-gestation result.

ectogenesis.title: Partial support versus normal development
ectogenesis.target: Physiological maintenance and growth during extrauterine fetal support
ectogenesis.species: Published ovine model; no local biological experiment
ectogenesis.hypothesis: Maintained physiological variables may coexist with impaired growth, so exchange performance and developmental outcomes require independent comparisons.
ectogenesis.endpoint: Source-reported growth and organ outcomes versus in-utero controls, support duration and missing follow-up.
ectogenesis.falsifier: A claimed normal-development result fails against the source's growth comparator or lacks the relevant outcome.
ectogenesis.structure_notes: Usuda et al. reported partial support up to 14 days with reduced somatic and organ growth compared with in-utero controls. This does not predict human outcomes.

evidence.value: Physiological maintenance with reduced somatic and organ growth
evidence.timepoint: Up to 14 days of partial support
evidence.notes: Source-reported animal evidence, not a local measurement or a continuous gestation demonstration.

reprogramming.title: Engineered vessel mutation-correction positive control
reprogramming.target: Pathogenic LMNA variant and vascular function
reprogramming.hypothesis: Correction of a known pathogenic LMNA variant can improve function in an engineered HGPS vascular model; this is a monogenic positive control, not a proxy for heterogeneous normal aging.
reprogramming.endpoint: Vasodilation, smooth-muscle density, perfusion and editing fraction, reported separately.
reprogramming.falsifier: Sequence correction does not improve the prespecified vessel function, or clonal/genomic outcomes worsen.
reprogramming.structure_notes: The published report describes restored vasodilation and smooth-muscle density. Some markers improved in constructs starting with at least 50% edited smooth-muscle cells. Confirm the source methods and exact comparator before quantitative reuse.

evidence.value: Restored vasodilation and smooth-muscle density; several markers improved when starting edited smooth-muscle fraction was at least 50%
evidence.notes: HGPS monogenic model. Does not establish editing age-acquired variants in ordinary aging.

reprogramming.title: Normal-aging clone-to-function evidence map
reprogramming.target: Age-associated somatic variants in a defined tissue and cell type
reprogramming.species: Human tissue datasets; model systems kept separate
reprogramming.tissue: Specify tissue and cell type before selecting variants
reprogramming.hypothesis: Only variants with causal, cell-type-specific functional effects and a measurable repair window should advance to correction models.
reprogramming.endpoint: Variant identity, clone fraction, causal perturbation evidence, cell coverage and tissue-relevant function.
reprogramming.falsifier: Variant burden or clone size does not predict functional impairment, or correction fails to improve function without harmful selection.
reprogramming.structure_notes: The cited six-person esophagus map is a tissue-specific observational starting point. A clone or mutation is not automatically harmful or a repair target.

tissues.title: Engineered cartilage functional comparator
tissues.target: Mature nasal-chondrocyte engineered cartilage for focal knee defects
tissues.hypothesis: A mature engineered construct may improve a patient-relevant cartilage outcome relative to an active comparator, while repair speed and durability remain separate endpoints.
tissues.endpoint: KOOS at 24 months, adjusted treatment difference, donor-site cost, graft integration and adverse healing.
tissues.falsifier: No clinically meaningful function difference, unacceptable donor-site morbidity or loss of repair durability.
tissues.structure_notes: The reported median KOOS was 85 versus 79 at 24 months; adjusted difference 7.27 points. This addresses focal defects, not diffuse osteoarthritis or systemic aging.

evidence.notes: Open-label active-comparator phase II trial for focal knee defects. Verify uncertainty interval and methods before reusing the estimate.

nanomedicine.title: Lung-targeted delivery cascade reference
nanomedicine.target: Lipid nanoparticle delivery of a CFTR base editor to lung basal stem cells
nanomedicine.species: Mouse model plus patient-derived airway cells in vitro
nanomedicine.tissue: Airway epithelium and lung basal stem cells
nanomedicine.hypothesis: Carrier accumulation must lead to intended-cell uptake, verified edit activity and restored airway function; each step needs a separate denominator.
nanomedicine.endpoint: Whole-lung distribution, target-cell editing fraction, allele outcomes, chloride function and persistence measured in matched models.
nanomedicine.falsifier: Organ signal without target-cell editing, or target-cell edits without functional rescue and acceptable off-target outcomes.
nanomedicine.study_design: Targeted delivery and functional assay study
nanomedicine.structure_notes: The cited report describes about 50% correction among isolated lung basal stem cells and restored chloride function in patient-derived airway cells in vitro; whole-lung editing was much lower. The long-persistence reporter result used a separate model.

evidence.value: About 50% editing in isolated lung basal stem cells; chloride function restored in patient-derived airway cells in vitro
evidence.unit: percent of isolated target cells; separate in-vitro function assay
evidence.timepoint: Model-specific; reporter persistence was measured separately
evidence.notes: Do not merge target-cell editing, whole-organ editing and persistence across separate models.

dental.title: Whole-tooth function reference and adult-cell gap
dental.hypothesis: The mouse organ-germ result supplies a functional reference; adult-human cell sourcing and controlled tooth architecture remain independent gaps.
dental.endpoint: Hardness, loading response, sensory response, root/ligament integration and durability.
dental.falsifier: Mineralized tissue fails loading or lacks functional host integration.
dental.structure_notes: Source reports functional mouse tooth replacement. It does not establish an adult-human bioidentical tooth or an available adult-human cell source.

evidence.comparator: Native tooth and source-defined assays; verify each assay separately
evidence.notes: Abstract-reviewed functional precedent; no pooled human inference.

dental.title: Human ameloblast organoid enamel-like material
dental.tissue: Enamel-like material in a non-dental graft site
dental.hypothesis: Mature ameloblast organoids can produce a useful enamel component; native prism architecture, bonding and loading require separate tests.
dental.endpoint: Mineral composition/architecture, enamel–dentin interface, hardness and repeated-load behavior.
dental.falsifier: Calcified deposits lack appropriate architecture, adhesion or mechanical function.
dental.evidence_stage: Human iPSC organoid and mouse graft
dental.study_design: Mechanistic organoid study with kidney-capsule grafts
dental.structure_notes: The 2026 primary source reports enamel-like calcified material, not an erupted tooth. Its reported GEO accessions are dataset leads, not downloaded or qualified data here.

evidence.value: Ameloblast maturation and enamel-like calcified material
evidence.timepoint: Source-defined assays; no human replacement follow-up
evidence.notes: Publisher full text accessed; no complete periodontal unit or human benefit inferred.

dental.title: Periodontal bone fill versus attachment benefit
dental.hypothesis: A cell-based construct may improve one outcome without an added attachment advantage over an active comparator.
dental.endpoint: Between-group clinical attachment, bone height, oriented attachment, mobility, adverse outcomes and follow-up.
dental.falsifier: Added cells do not improve the prespecified attachment endpoint or produce adverse integration.
dental.study_design: Contrast 2016 controlled PDLSC study and 2026 open-label ASC/PRP versus EMD study
dental.structure_notes: The 2026 abstract reports a bone-height advantage but no significant between-group attachment-gain difference, with 15 completers out of 21 recruited. The 2016 trial also reported no significant between-group bone-height difference. No claim of equivalence follows from nonsignificance. Full-text follow-up: three source observations retain the 2016 primary/secondary intervals and the 2025 pooled post hoc subgroup; verify their methods before saving.

evidence.value: No significant between-group clinical attachment-gain difference in the 2026 abstract
evidence.unit: comparison outcome, not proof of equivalence
evidence.notes: Open-label phase II abstract; attrition and patient/tooth units require full-text review before numerical synthesis.

evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.comparator: Cell group versus control with the shared regenerative treatment
evidence_records.outcome: Primary radiographic outcome: no significant between-group difference
evidence_records.value: Reported between-group p=0.742; both groups improved over time
evidence_records.unit: mm; source table labels mean +/- standard error
evidence_records.independent_unit: Teeth nested within patients; do not count teeth as independent patients
evidence_records.sample_size: 48 randomized teeth; 41 treated (20 cell, 21 control); 30 patients in the trial
evidence_records.notes: Full-text Methods and Table 2. Modified per-protocol analysis with last observation carried forward. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. Bone fill is a proxy, not functional ligament reconstruction.

evidence_records.source_title: PDLSC trial 2016: secondary clinical attachment outcome
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.outcome: Secondary clinical attachment comparison: no significant between-group difference
evidence_records.sample_size: 20 cell-group and 21 control-group teeth; not 41 independent patients
evidence_records.follow_up: 3 months for these clinical indices, not the 12-month radiographic interval
evidence_records.notes: Full-text efficacy assessment and Table 3. Retain this shorter outcome-specific interval. Clinical attachment level is not histologic proof of oriented cementum-ligament-bone attachment.

evidence_records.source_title: DPSC 2025: pooled post hoc stage-III attachment contrast
evidence_records.license: Primary source CC BY 4.0; this record is an attributed summary
evidence_records.stage_track: Post hoc combined dataset from two trials
evidence_records.comparator: DPSC versus saline in the pooled post hoc subgroup
evidence_records.outcome: Attachment-loss change favored DPSC in this subgroup
evidence_records.measure: Table 3: day-180 AL change from baseline; DPSC minus saline
evidence_records.unit: mm; negative change denotes reduced attachment loss
evidence_records.independent_unit: Methods specify tooth-level statistical analysis; patient/site dependence requires review
evidence_records.sample_size: Table 3 group n=54 and 40; not asserted to be independently replicated patients
evidence_records.notes: Full-text Clinical outcomes and Table 3. Post hoc pooling across trials is not prespecified overall primary confirmation. Source CI/sign retained; no re-estimation without raw data or covariance. No histologic or mechanical attachment restoration is inferred.

dental.title: Gingival coverage versus restored barrier
dental.hypothesis: A root-coverage signal can motivate further study but cannot establish a restored gingival barrier or complete periodontal unit.
dental.endpoint: Root coverage, tissue thickness/phenotype, barrier/seal function, inflammation and recurrence.
dental.falsifier: Coverage improves without the intended barrier function or does not persist.
dental.structure_notes: The abstract reports 14 cases with multiple sites and a root-coverage signal at six months. Sites must not be counted as independent patients. Whole-tooth or histological ligament regeneration is not established by this endpoint.

evidence.value: Root coverage reported; functional barrier/seal not established by the reviewed abstract
evidence.notes: Barrier remains unmeasured in this source scope despite the clinical coverage signal.

organoids.title: Qualified oxygen profiles before transport fitting
organoids.hypothesis: Measured local oxygen profiles can challenge the reduced sphere model only when geometry, source calibration and independent-unit splits are qualified.
organoids.endpoint: Measured spatial coverage, held-out units, assay calibration and later model error; no viability threshold inferred.
organoids.falsifier: Only gas settings, selected images or unlinked averaged profiles are available, or source units cross the validation split.
organoids.study_design: Source-linked intake; no new biological measurements
organoids.structure_notes: The sibling solver retains illustrative parameters and independent numerical checks. Intake is not fitting or biological validation.

organoids.title: Genome correction and construct function stay separate
organoids.target: Declared causal lesion in a stem-cell construct
organoids.hypothesis: A source-qualified intended edit may improve a specified construct function, while delivery coverage, unwanted products and clone behavior remain separate outcomes.
organoids.endpoint: Intended-only products, same-population target-cell coverage, functional comparator and durability.
organoids.falsifier: Correction is measured without useful function, or altered clone selection explains the apparent benefit.
organoids.structure_notes: The new sibling repo classifies classical conversion chemistry and audits source scope/count denominators. It does not select an editor or predict repair.

organoids.title: Ameloblast RNA comparisons and biological-unit gaps
organoids.species: Human-derived organoid RNA samples and a mixed fetal/iPSC reference
organoids.tissue: Ameloblast organoid transcriptome; functional enamel remains separate
organoids.hypothesis: Within-background molecular responses may support a maturation hypothesis after sample identity and independent culture provenance are qualified.
organoids.endpoint: Descriptive source-aligned CPM panel with library omission and pseudocount sensitivity; independent biological-unit qualification before inference
organoids.falsifier: Misaligned samples, unresolved clone or batch confounding, ambiguous tissue labels or a claim of a full factorial interaction without untreated-KO samples
organoids.evidence_stage: Retrieved public counts and computational descriptive comparison; tissue identity/function unqualified
organoids.study_design: Three source conditions with two labeled replicates each; genotype-by-treatment interaction is incomplete
organoids.structure_notes: GSE307437 supplies 41,129 unique gene rows in six source-aligned libraries. Descriptive CPM comparisons retain sparse enamel-associated rows and mixed molecular responses. Donor/clone/culture identities and reuse rights remain unqualified. Untreated KO is missing, so no full factorial interaction is estimated. GSE184749 pooling/tissue-label issues remain. See studies/dental-regeneration-2026-10-09/AMELOBLAST_EXPRESSION.md.

evidence.notes: Source-aligned counts analyzed descriptively; molecular changes do not certify functional tissue identity.
Expression and source labels cannot supply native enamel mechanical function.

evidence_records.source_title: GSE307437: calculated descriptive CPM marker contrasts
evidence_records.license: Dataset reuse license unqualified in this intake
evidence_records.stage_track: Computational descriptive analysis of deposited bulk RNA counts
evidence_records.developmental_interval: Source isAM organoid conditions; no adult tooth function assessed
evidence_records.comparator: WT treated versus WT untreated; knockout treated versus WT treated
evidence_records.outcome: Mixed molecular panel; identity and functional maturation remain unqualified
evidence_records.measure: CPM library means and log2(mean+1 CPM) contrast, calculated with the existing expression tool
evidence_records.value: WT treatment: DLX3 +1.093, SP6 +1.593, SOX2 -6.668; genotype under treatment: DLX3 -2.837, SP6 -4.070, SOX2 +7.120
evidence_records.independent_unit: Library; independent donor/clone/culture identities not established
evidence_records.sample_size: Two source-labeled replicate libraries per condition; not six independent donors
evidence_records.follow_up: Single source transcriptome comparison, not longitudinal tooth function
evidence_records.notes: Values are our descriptive calculation from source counts, not the paper's significance claims. Status refers to unqualified tissue identity. All eleven panel genes are retained in AMELOBLAST_EXPRESSION.md/ameloblast_expression_summary.json. ENAM is zero in both WT groups; low-count MMP20 changes strongly with pseudocount. No p values, batch adjustment or genotype-by-treatment interaction.

blueprints.title: Artificial wombs & ectogenesis
blueprints.query: artificial womb artificial placenta ectogenesis ex utero embryogenesis growth development
blueprints.question: Which biological functions and developmental transitions would a complete IVF-to-birth artificial gestation system have to support?
blueprints.who: Keep human embryo observations, mouse embryo culture, ovine fetal support and proposed human applications distinct.
blueprints.what: Implantation, placental formation, exchange, endocrine/immune interfaces, growth, maturation and transition to birth.
blueprints.where: A theoretical externally supported environment; wall power is one resource among exchange materials, monitoring and continuous support.
blueprints.when: Preserve each study's observed start/end developmental stages and follow-up instead of inferring a nine-month capability.
blueprints.why: Complete ectogenesis could reduce reliance on surrogate pregnancy if demonstrated; reduced congenital anomalies is a separate unproven hypothesis.
blueprints.how: Use the sibling artificial-womb-models evidence ledger and dimensionless fault fixtures; search primary sources here, retain contrary findings, and export reviewed campaign dossiers.
blueprints.falsifier: Failure at a developmental interface, reduced growth despite stable physiological variables, or unsupported transfer from animal or synthetic results to humans.
blueprints.desired_changes: Explore full artificial gestation as a long-term ambition while developing source-traceable models, observable engineering assumptions and independently reviewable software.

blueprints.title: Engineered tissues & repair
blueprints.query: engineered cartilage skin vascular graft functional clinical trial
blueprints.question: When does an engineered tissue restore durable function in an aging or damaged body?
blueprints.who: Keep human graft trials, perfused constructs and animal implants distinct.
blueprints.what: Engineered cartilage, skin, blood vessels and muscle with measurable structure and function.
blueprints.where: Vascular supply, extracellular matrix, host interface and immune compatibility.
blueprints.when: Early graft survival, healing speed and function months or years later are separate outcomes.
blueprints.why: Cell survival and a tissue-like shape do not guarantee mechanical or physiological function.
blueprints.how: Compare graft maturation, perfusion, donor-site demand, integration and patient-relevant function from primary trials and experimental tissue datasets.
blueprints.falsifier: A graft survives but heals slowly, loses function, scars or fails mechanical integration.
blueprints.desired_changes: Improve functional integration and durable repair, including tests of genome-corrected engineered tissue.

blueprints.title: Nanomedicine & tissue delivery
blueprints.query: targeted lipid nanoparticle base editing extrahepatic senolytic aged mice
blueprints.question: Can a carrier deliver enough active cargo to the intended aging tissue while limiting other-tissue exposure?
blueprints.who: Separate cultured human cells, aged animals and treated patients.
blueprints.what: Lipid nanoparticles, extracellular vesicles, liposomes and other targeted carriers for editors or damage-modifying cargo.
blueprints.where: Distinguish whole-organ accumulation, uptake by the intended cell type and intracellular cargo release.
blueprints.when: Measure hours-long distribution, weeks-long function and durable effects separately.
blueprints.why: A fluorescent carrier signal does not prove editing, selective senolysis or lasting rejuvenation.
blueprints.how: Compare biodistribution, target-cell editing or cargo activity, functional endpoints, dose-response and adverse observations in primary studies.
blueprints.falsifier: Target-organ fluorescence without target-cell action, or benefit offset by toxicity or poor coverage.
blueprints.desired_changes: Improve tissue and cell targeting with reproducible functional readouts and explicit delivery gaps.

blueprints.title: Glycation & tissue resilience
blueprints.question: Can carbonyl stress be reduced while preserving useful signaling and tissue function?
blueprints.who: Compare healthy adults, metabolic disease cohorts, cells and animal models separately.
blueprints.what: Carnosine and related histidine-containing dipeptides; carbonyl scavenging and glycation hypotheses.
blueprints.where: Circulating markers versus long-lived extracellular matrix; tissue exposure is a separate question.
blueprints.when: Distinguish prevention of new damage from reversal of established damage.
blueprints.why: Lower circulating glycation markers might not remove existing tissue crosslinks.
blueprints.how: Retrieve human and mechanistic studies; resolve carnosine, anserine and homocarnosine; compare structures and conformer sensitivity.
blueprints.falsifier: Biomarker changes without measurable improvement in the tissue endpoint, or no exposure at the target tissue.
blueprints.desired_changes: Explore stability and polarity hypotheses while keeping carbonyl-reactive chemistry under scrutiny.

blueprints.title: Muscle & metabolic tradeoffs
blueprints.question: Which metabolic improvements are compatible with preserving muscle mass and training adaptation?
blueprints.who: Keep older-adult training trials distinct from healthy young adults and people with diabetes.
blueprints.what: Metformin, mTOR/AMPK signaling, incretin therapies and muscle outcomes.
blueprints.where: Skeletal muscle, liver and systemic metabolic regulation.
blueprints.when: Acute signaling versus adaptation over months; longevity remains a separate endpoint.
blueprints.why: An intervention can improve one endpoint while impairing another.
blueprints.how: Compare randomized body-composition and training studies, lean mass, strength and physical function; retain null and adverse outcomes.
blueprints.falsifier: Improved metabolic markers paired with loss of strength, lean tissue or training responsiveness.
blueprints.desired_changes: Separate desired metabolic effects from muscle-growth suppression; no single anti-aging score.

blueprints.title: Metabolic aging & brain health
blueprints.query: metabolic aging cognitive decline GLP-1 randomized
blueprints.question: Do metabolic interventions preserve cognitive function with age, and is the proposed mechanism tested?
blueprints.who: People with diabetes or obesity, neurodegenerative disease models, and healthy adults are separate populations.
blueprints.what: Metabolic, vascular and inflammatory interventions with objective cognitive and disease endpoints.
blueprints.where: Brain exposure, peripheral metabolism and inflammatory signaling.
blueprints.when: Transient subjective effects versus durable cognitive performance or disease incidence.
blueprints.why: Reduced glucose variability is a mechanism hypothesis, not proof of cognitive enhancement.
blueprints.how: Retrieve trials and observational studies; separate test performance from dementia diagnosis; collect anecdotes with cointerventions and identity uncertainty.
blueprints.falsifier: Association disappears after confounder control, or no functional benefit despite biomarker change.
blueprints.desired_changes: Investigate exposure and selectivity hypotheses; descriptors alone cannot predict brain penetration.

blueprints.title: Senescence & immune clearance
blueprints.question: Can harmful senescent cells be cleared while preserving beneficial senescence and tissue repair?
blueprints.who: Aged and disease-model animals first; human evidence must be identified independently.
blueprints.what: uPAR-directed CAR-T, senolytic small molecules and senomorphic approaches.
blueprints.where: Target antigen distribution across tissues and cell states.
blueprints.when: Durability, recurrence of senescence and long-term immune consequences.
blueprints.why: A shared marker may be present on cells that should be preserved.
blueprints.how: Map primary studies, target-expression datasets and functional endpoints; inspect selectivity and adverse observations.
blueprints.falsifier: Off-target cell loss, impaired repair, or senescence-marker reduction without functional benefit.
blueprints.desired_changes: Improve tissue and cell-state specificity as a research objective; no engineered-cell construction protocol.

blueprints.title: Somatic mutations & genome repair
blueprints.query: somatic mutation aging tissues base editing functional repair
blueprints.question: Which age-acquired DNA changes impair tissue function, and what fraction of affected cells would need correction to recover it?
blueprints.who: Compare normal human tissues, disease models and edited patients by age and cell type.
blueprints.what: Somatic single-base variants, indels, clone behavior, base-editing evidence and epigenetic state as a parallel variable.
blueprints.where: Map mutation classes and clonal burden by tissue and cell type; mitochondrial DNA is a separate target.
blueprints.when: Distinguish prevention of new mutations, correction of existing ones and long-term clonal selection.
blueprints.why: Epigenetic reprogramming changes cell state but does not itself rewrite a mutated DNA base.
blueprints.how: Connect single-cell mutation maps to measured cell phenotypes; compare target coverage, delivery fraction, editing fraction and functional rescue across primary studies.
blueprints.falsifier: Sequence correction without functional rescue, or selection and off-target changes that worsen tissue outcomes.
blueprints.desired_changes: Prioritize causal lesions and tissue function while tracking genome and epigenome independently.

blueprints.title: Replacement organs & integration
blueprints.query: bioprinted kidney liver vascularization functional transplantation
blueprints.question: What prevents printed or grown tissue from replacing a full-size functional organ?
blueprints.who: Organoids, engineered constructs, animal transplantation and human recipients are distinct stages.
blueprints.what: Bioprinting, vascularization, maturation, immune compatibility and transplant integration.
blueprints.where: Perfusion, collecting systems, nerves and interfaces with host tissue.
blueprints.when: Viability in culture versus months of stable integrated organ function.
blueprints.why: Correct geometry and cell survival do not establish complete organ function.
blueprints.how: Link primary datasets to the existing oxygen/perfusion tools; model transport with explicit measured or illustrative parameters.
blueprints.falsifier: Necrotic regions, incomplete maturation, thrombosis or failure of the organ-specific functional endpoint.
blueprints.desired_changes: Improve transport, architecture and integration independently; robotic transplantation remains a separate engineering program.

blueprints.title: Skin, hair & structural restoration
blueprints.query: scar regeneration skin appendages wound healing
blueprints.question: Can tissue be restored with normal architecture and appendages rather than only a changed visual appearance?
blueprints.who: Human clinical studies, animal wound models and engineered tissues remain separate.
blueprints.what: Scar remodeling, skin regeneration, hair follicles, dental structures and aesthetic restoration.
blueprints.where: Epidermis, dermis, extracellular matrix, appendages and supporting structures.
blueprints.when: Early closure versus mature scarring and long-term durability.
blueprints.why: Scarless appearance and complete biological restoration are different endpoints.
blueprints.how: Retrieve source-specific images, histology and functional measures; track applicability across injury types and ages.
blueprints.falsifier: Improved appearance with impaired barrier function, abnormal architecture or recurrence.
blueprints.desired_changes: Compare cosmetic, structural and functional outcomes independently.

blueprints.title: Experimental compound leads
blueprints.query: experimental geroprotector epitalon thymalin clinical trial
blueprints.question: Which informal claims can be turned into specific, falsifiable research hypotheses?
blueprints.who: Record species, population and whether a report is self-described.
blueprints.what: Epitalon, thymalin, SARMs and other user-selected experimental leads.
blueprints.where: Specify the proposed tissue and measurable endpoint for each claim.
blueprints.when: Immediate subjective effects versus persistent objective effects.
blueprints.why: Forum and vendor reports can reveal questions while containing selection, commercial and identity biases.
blueprints.how: Search literature, registries and public web leads; preserve source type, missing information, cointerventions and contradictory reports.
blueprints.falsifier: No objective signal, unverified compound identity, duplicated anecdotes or results limited to a different population.
blueprints.desired_changes: Explore structural neighbors and submitted modifications; retain rejected candidates and unknowns.

blueprints.title: Teeth, gums & periodontal attachment
blueprints.query: tooth regeneration periodontal ligament gingival stem cells functional comparator
blueprints.question: Which components of a bioidentical tooth and its supporting tissues have direct functional evidence, and what remains missing?
blueprints.who: Keep human trials, human-derived constructs in mice and embryonic mouse tooth-germ studies separate.
blueprints.what: Enamel, dentin, living pulp, cementum, periodontal ligament, alveolar bone and gingival barrier as distinct outcomes.
blueprints.where: Restore the tooth-root/ligament/bone interface and gingival seal; avoid conflating bone fill with attachment.
blueprints.when: Development, eruption, early healing, loading and long-term durability are separate intervals.
blueprints.why: A calcified deposit or improved radiograph does not establish a complete innervated, load-bearing replacement tooth.
blueprints.how: Compare primary sources, intended tissue identity, controlled functional outcomes, adverse healing and donor/site dependence. Retain inconclusive and negative comparisons.
blueprints.falsifier: Mineral deposition without native-like architecture, ankylosis instead of ligament attachment, loss under load, impaired gum barrier or no advantage over the declared comparator.
blueprints.desired_changes: Build a component-level roadmap toward bioidentical tooth and periodontal restoration without upgrading partial endpoints to whole-organ regeneration.

blueprints.title: Organoids & stem-cell construct function
blueprints.query: organoid stem cell functional maturation oxygen profile independent donor validation
blueprints.question: Does a specified stem-cell construct reproduce a useful tissue function beyond morphology and marker expression?
blueprints.who: Declare species, donor, clone, culture and assay hierarchy; cultured human cells are not treated patients.
blueprints.what: Cell identity, maturation, transport, genome stability and tissue-specific function, measured independently.
blueprints.where: Local oxygen and nutrient transport, host interfaces and spatial organization.
blueprints.when: Formation, maturation, transplantation and persistence remain separate intervals.
blueprints.why: A reproducible image or marker panel does not establish useful organ function or transplant integration.
blueprints.how: Use source-qualified datasets, donor/culture-aware comparators and the independent organoid-oxygen-lab methods. Record model assumptions and measurement gaps.
blueprints.falsifier: Markers improve without function, construct selection explains the apparent effect, or transport/genome stability fails despite morphology.
blueprints.desired_changes: Connect qualified measurements to reproducible analyses while retaining organ-specific function and genome integrity as separate outcomes.

findings.title: Fetal lambs received weeks of partial extrauterine support
findings.claim: Partridge et al. reported support of already-developed fetal lambs for up to 28 days, with growth and organ maturation during the supported interval.
findings.boundary: Development began in pregnant ewes. This is partial support, not IVF-to-birth gestation or a demonstrated human benefit.

findings.title: Mouse embryo culture covered an early post-implantation interval
findings.claim: Aguilera-Castrejon et al. cultured natural mouse post-implantation embryos from E5.5 to E11 for up to six days, spanning pre-gastrulation to advanced organogenesis.
findings.boundary: No complete gestation or live birth was demonstrated. This early interval cannot be joined to lamb support as evidence of a continuous system.

findings.title: Physiological maintenance coexisted with reduced growth
findings.claim: Usuda et al. reported partial support of premature ovine fetuses for up to 14 days, with largely maintained physiological variables but reduced somatic and organ growth compared with in-utero controls.
findings.boundary: Exchange or circulation stability does not by itself establish normal development. These are animal observations, not human predictions.

findings.title: FDA discussion concerned support for extreme prematurity
findings.claim: The 2023 FDA advisory discussion addressed devices intended to bridge extremely premature birth to later gestation, including animal-model limits and developmental follow-up.
findings.boundary: An official development discussion is not clinical trial evidence, regulatory approval, or a complete-gestation demonstration.

findings.title: BCNatal reported a 21-day animal milestone in 2026
findings.claim: Hospital Clinic's July 2026 fetaLife update reported 21 days of ovine support and follow-up of one sheep beyond one year; a first human study was described as planned for 2028-2029.
findings.boundary: This is an institutional announcement, not a human result or a newly assessed peer-reviewed dataset. Planned dates remain conditional; complete ectogenesis was not demonstrated.

findings.title: Carnosine: a positive biomarker result
findings.claim: A randomized study in 54 adults with type 2 diabetes reported improvements in circulating carboxymethyl lysine and HbA1c over 12 weeks.
findings.boundary: No demonstrated reversal of established tissue crosslinks or human aging.

findings.title: Carnosine: a null result in a different population
findings.claim: A randomized study in 36 autistic children found no significant change in measured plasma AGE or lipoxidation-precursor concentrations.
findings.boundary: Different population and study conditions; this is not a direct replication of the diabetes study.

findings.title: Metformin can conflict with a muscle endpoint
findings.claim: The MASTERS trial in 94 adults aged 65 and older found smaller lean and thigh muscle mass gains during resistance training with metformin; strength differences were not significant.
findings.boundary: This does not establish the effect in younger healthy adults.

findings.title: Tirzepatide: fat loss also included lean tissue
findings.claim: In the 160-participant SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy, fat mass fell 33.9% and lean mass 10.9%; about one quarter of lost weight was lean mass.
findings.boundary: DXA lean tissue includes water and nonmuscle tissues. This is not evidence of muscle anabolism.

findings.title: A cognition lead, with causal uncertainty
findings.claim: A retrospective diabetes-cohort analysis reported a lower dementia hazard with tirzepatide than semaglutide: HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-0.99.
findings.boundary: Observational diagnosis data do not establish cognitive enhancement or mediation by glucose variability.

findings.title: Senolytic CAR-T has functional mouse evidence
findings.claim: uPAR-targeting CAR-T cells improved exercise capacity and glucose tolerance in aged or metabolically stressed mouse models.
findings.boundary: The study does not demonstrate human rejuvenation or universal target selectivity.

findings.title: OSK: tissue-specific functional recovery
findings.claim: Mouse retinal studies reported axon regeneration and recovery of visual function with OSK expression in injury, glaucoma and aging models.
findings.boundary: Not whole-body reversal and not evidence that accumulated DNA-sequence mutations were repaired.

findings.title: Transient reprogramming can also produce tumors
findings.claim: A separate in-vivo mouse reprogramming study produced tumors containing undifferentiated dysplastic cells.
findings.boundary: Different constructs and experimental conditions from targeted recovery studies; model identity matters.

findings.title: Epithalamin: a striking but narrow historical clinical signal
findings.claim: A randomized comparative follow-up of 39 older coronary patients given epithalamin and 40 controls reported lower cardiovascular aging measures and 28% fewer deaths after 12 years.
findings.boundary: Small, older, disease-specific study from one research program; the abstract does not give enough design detail to evaluate allocation, attrition or independent replication. Epithalamin extract evidence cannot automatically be assigned to synthetic Epitalon or vendor products.

findings.title: Epitalon extends telomeres in cell models, including cancer lines
findings.claim: A 2025 study reported telomere extension and telomerase changes in normal epithelial and fibroblast lines, and telomere extension associated with ALT activity in two breast cancer cell lines.
findings.boundary: Cell-culture finding only; no whole-body aging outcome. The journal later corrected Figures 1-3 (PMID 41240216), so the corrected article and methods should be checked before interpreting magnitudes.

findings.title: Thymalin and Epithalamin: historical mortality claims need design review
findings.claim: A 2003 report describes clinical observations of thymic and pineal peptide bioregulators in 266 older people and reports lower mortality across treatment groups over 6-8 years.
findings.boundary: The abstract does not describe randomization or enough methods to assess confounding and attrition; products were peptide bioregulators, not evidence for every modern synthetic or vendor-labeled peptide.

findings.title: Enobosarm increased lean mass in a short phase II trial
findings.claim: A 12-week double-blind phase II trial in 120 healthy men over 60 and postmenopausal women reported dose-dependent lean-mass gains and an improvement in physical function for GTx-024 (enobosarm).
findings.boundary: One investigational molecule and a short trial in older adults; it does not establish effects in young bodybuilders or the long-term safety of enobosarm or other SARMs. The sponsor employed a study author.

findings.title: FDA warning covers products marketed as SARMs
findings.claim: FDA states SARMs are not approved and describes reports of serious or life-threatening events, including liver injury and cardiovascular risks.
findings.boundary: Regulatory safety information is not a molecule-specific trial; online product identity and purity add uncertainty.

findings.title: Retatrutide has phase III diabetes results
findings.claim: In a 40-week randomized phase III trial of 537 adults with type 2 diabetes, retatrutide reduced HbA1c and mean bodyweight fell 11.5-15.3% across treatment groups, versus 2.6% with placebo.
findings.boundary: The population had type 2 diabetes and inadequate control with diet and exercise alone. The trial did not establish muscle anabolism, cognitive enhancement or slower aging.

findings.title: Base editing corrected the causal progeria mutation in mice
findings.claim: An adenine base editor corrected the LMNA mutation in patient-derived cells and HGPS mice; treatment at postnatal day 14 extended median lifespan in one mouse cohort from 215 to 510 days.
findings.boundary: This corrects one known, high-effect mutation in a rare accelerated-aging disease model. It does not demonstrate repair of the diverse somatic mutations accumulated in ordinary aging or human rejuvenation.

findings.title: Progeria bone editing showed a narrow timing window
findings.claim: A September 2026 HGPS mouse study reported partial bone rescue; mutation correction was about 22% after treatment at postnatal day 14, about 10% at one month and below 1% at four months.
findings.boundary: A monogenic progeria model and AAV9-delivered editor; the timing dependence highlights delivery and disease-stage limits for translation to ordinary aging.

findings.title: NSI-189 phase II: a mixed cognitive signal
findings.claim: In a 220-participant randomized phase II trial in major depressive disorder, NSI-189 did not significantly improve the primary depression endpoint versus placebo. Some CogScreen secondary measures favored one treatment arm, while Cogstate measures did not show a corresponding signal.
findings.boundary: This was a depression-treatment study, not a trial of healthy-person cognitive enhancement; secondary test findings need prespecified replication.

findings.title: A kidney scaffold maintained blood perfusion for seven days
findings.claim: In a small porcine study, re-endothelialized decellularized kidney grafts averaged 87.7%, 80.9% and 68.5% perfusion on days 0, 3 and 7, respectively; native-kidney controls averaged 98.4%. The differences were not statistically significant.
findings.boundary: This measured vascular patency, not filtration or replacement-kidney function. It does not establish durable graft integration or stable endothelial coverage.

findings.title: Human kidney cells enabled short-term filtration in a pig graft
findings.claim: Human endothelial cells and podocytes repopulated a decellularized porcine kidney scaffold. In heterotopic pig implants, grafts produced urine with filtration indices; the longest reported observation was five hours in one graft.
findings.boundary: Acute proof of concept with very small numbers. The constructs lacked tubular epithelial cells, so tubular reabsorption and full kidney function were not tested; the grafts did not replace the animals' native kidneys.

findings.title: Follicle transplantation remodeled some mature human scars
findings.claim: A small human pilot found epidermal and dermal remodeling after anagen hair-follicle transplantation in three people with mature scalp scars; a separate split-thickness skin-graft scar was also examined.
findings.boundary: Very small, localized, non-randomized pilot evidence. It does not establish scarless healing, complete scar removal, or restoration of youthful appearance or function across other scar types.

findings.title: uPAR CAR-T also has a distinct preclinical oncology signal
findings.claim: A 2026 study reported that uPAR-directed CAR-T cells attacked malignant and supportive stromal populations across preclinical solid-tumor models, with activity in humanized-mouse systems.
findings.boundary: This is preclinical oncology evidence, not a human treatment result and not evidence that broad uPAR targeting is safe for senescent-cell clearance in aging tissues.

findings.title: Caloric restriction reduced mutation burden in some mouse tissues
findings.claim: Duplex sequencing of 36 mice at 19 months found about 29% fewer somatic substitutions in bulk liver, 15% fewer in kidney and 39% fewer in hepatocytes under caloric restriction; the neuron contrast was not significant.
findings.boundary: This measured mutation prevention or accumulation, not correction of existing variants. The two restricted-feeding schedules differed in reported lifespan but not detectably in substitution burden; mutation reduction alone does not explain longevity.

findings.title: Age-related clones have different cellular phenotypes
findings.claim: Joint single-cell DNA and RNA profiling of phenotypically normal aged esophagus from six people linked NOTCH1-mutant clones to stunted epithelial differentiation and TP53-mutant clones to increased cycling and altered differentiation.
findings.boundary: Small, tissue-specific observational map. A mutation or expanding clone is not automatically a damage target; causal tissue-level benefit from editing these clones was not tested.

findings.title: Clinical base correction: one monogenic case, short follow-up
findings.claim: A patient-specific lipid-nanoparticle base editor was given to an infant with CPS1 deficiency. Over seven weeks after initial treatment, more dietary protein was tolerated and nitrogen-scavenger medication was halved.
findings.boundary: One infant with a known inherited mutation, not age-acquired genome damage. No human tissue-editing fraction or long-term rejuvenation outcome was reported.

findings.title: Full reprogramming does not erase somatic sequence variants
findings.claim: Sequencing of human induced-pluripotent-stem-cell clones found substantial somatic variation, including pre-existing mutations and selection of cancer-associated variants during culture.
findings.boundary: Cultured full reprogramming is not the same as partial in-vivo epigenetic reprogramming. It illustrates why genome sequence and epigenetic state need separate measurements.

findings.title: Mature engineered cartilage improved a two-year knee outcome
findings.claim: In a randomized phase II trial of focal knee defects, mature nasal-chondrocyte engineered cartilage produced a median KOOS of 85 versus 79 for a less-mature cell-activated matrix at 24 months; the adjusted difference was 7.27 points.
findings.boundary: An open-label active-comparator trial for focal defects, not reversal of diffuse osteoarthritis or whole-body aging. The patient-reported score does not alone establish lifelong graft durability.

findings.title: Engineered skin improved scar quality but closed more slowly
findings.claim: In a 23-person intra-patient randomized phase II trial, bio-engineered autologous skin had a better observer scar score at three months (23.4 versus 27.9) and greater coverage per donor area (8.5 versus 0.9) than split-thickness grafts.
findings.boundary: Median wound closure took 60.5 versus 22 days, and early graft take was 69.8% versus 85.0%. This is reconstruction of defects, not scar-free or age-reversed skin.
findings.design: Human randomized intra-patient phase II trial

findings.title: Corrected progeria cells restored functions in engineered vessels
findings.claim: Base-edited patient-derived vascular cells yielded perfused tissue-engineered vessels with restored vasodilation and smooth-muscle density; constructs starting with at least 50% edited smooth-muscle cells improved several markers.
findings.boundary: An in-vitro human tissue model of one monogenic accelerated-aging disorder. It does not show transplantation, correction of normal age-acquired mutations or clinical vascular rejuvenation.

findings.title: Lung-targeted nanoparticles delivered base correction to stem cells
findings.claim: Intravenous lipid nanoparticles corrected a CFTR mutation in about 50% of isolated lung basal stem cells in a mouse model and restored chloride function in patient-derived airway cells in vitro.
findings.boundary: The whole-lung editing fraction was much lower than the isolated stem-cell fraction. The long 660-day persistence result used a separate reporter model, not demonstrated long-term rescue of mutant CFTR or aging damage.

findings.title: A nanosenolytic improved short-term function in aged mice
findings.claim: An experimental nanoparticle senolytic lowered senescence-associated signals in liver, lung and kidney and improved treadmill and grip measures in 18-month-old mice over an eight-week experiment.
findings.boundary: Physical-function groups were small (n=5). Carrier biodistribution signal is not proof of selective intracellular action, and no human or lifespan benefit was shown.

findings.title: Targeted vesicles carried senolytics to aged adipose tissue
findings.claim: Peptide-functionalized extracellular vesicles carrying dasatinib and quercetin reduced adipose inflammatory signals and produced modest physical-performance improvements in naturally aged mice.
findings.boundary: Small, short animal study; vesicle localization does not itself establish cargo release or target-cell selectivity. No maximal-speed improvement, human outcome or longevity result was shown.

findings.title: Bioengineered retinal implant reached older patients
findings.claim: A phase I/IIa study implanted a stem-cell-derived retinal-pigment-epithelium monolayer on a scaffold in 15 older adults with advanced geographic atrophy; four treated eyes gained more than five visual-acuity letters at one year.
findings.boundary: Single-arm safety study with a non-significant fellow-eye comparison, not demonstrated efficacy. Serious ocular events occurred in early recipients; tissue implantation did not restore normal vision.

findings.title: Brain-endothelial nanosenolytic changed barrier markers in aged rats
findings.claim: In naturally aged rats, a navitoclax-loaded senescence-responsive nanoparticle reduced brain-endothelial senescence markers and blood-brain-barrier leakage and improved an exploratory-behavior measure versus vehicle.
findings.boundary: Small animal groups, a behavioral surrogate rather than proven cognitive recovery, and unresolved local-versus-systemic mechanism. Lower administered payload across different routes does not establish a 250-fold safety gain; no lifespan or human outcome was measured.

findings.title: Human ameloblast organoids produced an enamel component
findings.claim: The 2026 source reports enamel-like calcified material after human-derived ameloblast organoids were grafted under a mouse kidney capsule.
findings.boundary: This is component-level evidence, not an erupted human tooth or a functioning periodontal unit.
findings.design: Human iPSC organoid / mouse graft; publisher text accessed

findings.title: Bone-height advantage did not establish added attachment gain
findings.claim: The 2026 ASC/PRP trial abstract reports greater bone height than EMD but no significant between-group clinical attachment-gain difference.
findings.boundary: Fifteen of 21 recruited patients completed the study. Attrition and endpoint-specific uncertainty need review; nonsignificance is not equivalence.
findings.design: Human open-label phase II; abstract reviewed

findings.title: A controlled PDLSC comparison retained a null between-group result
findings.claim: The 2016 trial reported bone-height improvement in both groups without a significant between-group difference.
findings.boundary: Within-group improvement cannot establish an added-cell effect or complete functional periodontal attachment.
findings.design: Human randomized trial; primary full text reviewed

findings.title: Deposited dental RNA shows mixed, count-sensitive molecular responses
findings.claim: Descriptive CPM analysis of 41,129 gene rows in six GSE307437 libraries finds DLX3/SP6 shifts alongside sparse enamel-associated rows and pseudocount-sensitive effects.
findings.boundary: Unknown donor/clone/culture independence, composition-sensitive normalization and missing untreated KO prevent causal interaction or donor-heldout claims. Expression does not establish native enamel or tooth function.
findings.design: Source-aligned computational descriptive comparison; no significance testing
